category_title: Highly verbal preschoolers who talk out of turn during group activities
minimal_context: Sybil is participating in a large group circle time discussion where the class is sharing weekend stories.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Welcome to circle time, everyone. Today we are going to share our favorite things we did over the weekend. Who would like to go first?

STUDENT: I went to the zoo with my family and we saw the monkeys and they were swinging everywhere and making funny noises!

TUTOR: Thank you for sharing. Let's see what Sarah did.

STUDENT: And after the monkeys we saw the lions but they were just sleeping in the sun, so we went to get pretzels!

TUTOR: Sarah, it is your turn to speak now.

STUDENT: I like pretzels with cheese! Sarah, did you get pretzels too? My dad said we can go back next week and see the elephants!

options.A: Closely observe Sybil's interests and current understandings each day, then build the circle time curriculum for the next week based on those observations.
options.B: Observe the occurrences of Sybil's target behavior during circle time, recording the data in scatter plots and ABC charts when the session finishes.
options.C: Before circle time begins, use pictures to remind Sybil to raise her hand before speaking and wait her turn to talk.
options.D: Compromise and negotiate situations with Sybil, sharing decisions and power during circle time discussions instead of imposing adult control.
